title: Constructible sheaves over a finite ring have etale origin
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme and $B$ a finite commutative ring. For the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] of the small pro-etale and etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, and the constructibility notions [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] and [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], pullback $\nu_T^*$ induces an equivalence between constructible sheaves of $B$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and intrinsically constructible sheaves of $B$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (locally constant with finite module stalks on a finite partition by locally closed constructible subschemes).

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible; global finite-stratification refinement using restriction compatibility and finite locally constant comparison (lemma-compare-locally-constant, Tag 099Y). No qcqs assumption on T is imposed.

proof.text:
Let $G$ be a constructible etale $B$-module sheaf, with its finite global partition $i_k:S_k	o T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], its finite constant values give locally constant restrictions with finite stalks. The isomorphism $i_{k,\mathrm{proet}}^*
u_T^*G\cong
u_{S_k}^*i_{k,\mathrm{Et}}^*G$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and clause (a) of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] show that each restriction of $
u_T^*G$ is lisse. The same partition, with the same subscheme structures, therefore witnesses intrinsic constructibility. No affine-local-to-global constructibility criterion is used.

proof.text: Write $F_T=\nu_T^*$ and $R_T=\nu_{T,*}$. The unit $\eta_G:G\to R_TF_TG$ is invertible for every etale $B$-module sheaf by [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]. The adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(F_TG,F_TH)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(G,R_TF_TH)$, and postcomposition with $\eta_H^{-1}$ identifies the latter with $\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$. Thus $F_T$ is fully faithful on all module sheaves. Call a pro-etale sheaf classical if it is isomorphic to $F_TG$ for some etale sheaf. It is classical exactly when its counit $\epsilon_P:F_TR_TP\to P$ is invertible: one implication takes $G=R_TP$, and the other uses naturality and the triangle identity $\epsilon_{F_TG}\circ F_T\eta_G=1$. In particular fully faithful $F_T$ lifts an isomorphism between two of its images uniquely, together with the inverse.

Being classical is Zariski-local. For an open immersion $v:V\to T$, restriction of a pro-etale sheaf is evaluation on objects over $V$, by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. The explicit direct-image formula in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] consequently gives $(R_TP)|_V=R_V(P|_V)$: both evaluate to $P(W)$ for etale $W\to V$. Together with [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], this identifies $\epsilon_P|_V$ with $\epsilon_{P|_V}$, since the evaluation counit and its adjoint restriction are the same maps. If $P$ is classical on an open cover, these restricted counits are invertible by step 2. The open family is a pro-etale cover: its pullbacks cover each affine object, and quasi-compactness of that object supplies a finite subcover by quasi-compact affine opens. Locality for covering families, clause (1) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative], then makes $\epsilon_P$ invertible globally. Only covering locality is used, never conservativity of geometric stalks on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

proof.text: Classical $B$-module sheaves are closed under extensions. For $0\to F_TG'\to P\to F_TG''\to0$, [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] gives its distinguished triangle with boundary $\delta:F_TG''\to(F_TG')[1]$. Exactness of $F_T$ follows from [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]; [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] makes its termwise derived functor triangulated. Full faithfulness on $D^+$ in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] uniquely lifts $\delta$ to $\varphi:G''\to G'[1]$, since both arguments are bounded below. By TR1 and inverse rotation TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category], choose a triangle in $D^+$ (which is closed under shifts and cones) $G'\to H\to G''\xrightarrow{\varphi}G'[1]$. Rotate its image and the triangle of the extension to start with $\delta$, and apply TR3 with identities on the first two objects. [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] gives $F_TH\cong P$. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] shows $H$ has zero cohomology outside degree zero; by [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single], $H\cong G[0]$ for $G=H^0(H)$. Applying $H^0$ gives an isomorphism of sheaves $F_TG\cong P$, since exactness computes $H^0(F_TG[0])=F_TG$. No constructibility of $G$ is claimed at this step.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, extension argument; derived full faithfulness and lifting the extension boundary

proof.text:
Prove by induction on $N\geq0$, for every scheme $Y$, that every pro-etale $B$-module sheaf $P$ lisse on a finite constructible locally closed partition with at most $N$ nonempty strata is classical. If $N=0$, $Y$ is empty and the sheaf is the zero sheaf, namely $
u_Y^*0$. If $N=1$, the immersion of the unique nonempty stratum has image all of $Y$; it need not be an isomorphism. Avoid assuming otherwise: use the local argument below with its closed-stratum restriction, which applies for every $N\geq1$. Given $y\in Y_k$, [lem-sf-constructible-partition-local-closed-stratum] supplies affine open $V
i y$ where $S_k\cap V$ is closed and $U=V\setminus(S_k\cap V)$ is quasi-compact. Give each restricted stratum the fibre-product structure $S_i	imes_Y V$, not an arbitrary factorization through $V$. Restrictions of lisse sheaves to these open subschemes are lisse: restrict their trivializing covers and constant values; geometric stalks on an open are the same stalks. The immersion $i:Z=S_k	imes_YV	o V$ is closed: by [def-weil-closed-immersion] an immersion is locally a closed immersion in an open neighbourhood of its image. Since its image here is closed in $V$, cover $V$ by that neighbourhood and its image complement; the structure-sheaf map is surjective on the former and has zero target on the latter, so it is surjective everywhere. Together with the closed topological embedding this is the definition of closed immersion, and $j:U	o V$ is quasi-compact because $V$ is affine and $U$ is quasi-compact. On $U$ the remaining strata have at most $N-1$ nonempty members, so induction gives $j^*P_V\cong
u_U^*G_U$. On $Z$, $i^*P_V$ is lisse, so clause (b) of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] gives $i^*P_V\cong
u_Z^*G_Z$. By [lem-sf-proetale-open-closed-sequence], $0	o j_!j^*P_V	o P_V	o i_*i^*P_V	o0$ is exact. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] its first term is $
u_V^*(j_!G_U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] a closed immersion is affine, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact and quasi-separated; [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] applied to $G_Z[0]\in D^+$ and followed by $H^0$ identifies its last term with $
u_V^*(i_*G_Z)$. The degree-zero identification follows from [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero]: direct image is left exact, being a right adjoint, and these small-site module sheaf categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], hence have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Thus both end terms are classical. Step 4 makes $P_V$ classical and step 3 makes $P$ classical. When $U$ is empty the first term is zero; the argument still applies.

proof.text:
Let $P$ be intrinsically constructible, and choose $G$ with $
u_T^*G\cong P$ by step 5. Retain the original global finite partition $i_k:S_k	o T$ of $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], $
u_{S_k}^*(i_k^{-1}G)\cong i_k^*P$. Clause (b) of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] gives a lisse etale sheaf $H_k$ with $
u_{S_k}^*H_k\cong i_k^*P$. Full faithfulness from step 2, applied on $S_k$, lifts the resulting isomorphism to $i_k^{-1}G\cong H_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], each $H_k$ admits etale local trivializations with finite constant $B$-module values. Thus precisely the original partition witnesses constructibility of $G$ in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Combined with preservation in step 1 and full faithfulness in step 2, this proves the asserted equivalence. The argument works for arbitrary $T$, the zero finite ring, zero sheaves, and empty strata; it neither replaces $B$ by a valuation-ring quotient nor equates global finite partitions with affine-local constructibility.

split_report.summary: Preserves the arbitrary finite-ring and arbitrary-scheme statement. Reuses finite-ring lisse comparison, local closed-stratum induction, open/closed comparison and derived extension lifting. Steps 1, 5, and 6 use clauses (a) and (b) for arbitrary finite commutative rings on strata; the unit comparison nodes do not give locally constant descent.
Step 1 identifies the intrinsic target subcategory through its actual global partition definition; no proper-base-change statement supplies this definition.

Step 4 uses TR1, TR2 and TR3 to complete and compare the lifted boundary triangles; these are the defining generic triangulated-category axioms.
